title: Morphisms in a left localization are a colimit of ordinary Hom sets
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $S$ a multiplicative system, and $Q:\mathcal C\to S^{-1}\mathcal C$ its left localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For objects $X,Y$ of $\mathcal C$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_{s:X\to I\,\in S}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(Y,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{S^{-1}\mathcal C}(Q(Y),Q(X))$ in the usual left-localization orientation is a bijection; equivalently, morphisms in $S^{-1}\mathcal C$ are represented by postcomposition along arrows of $S$ and identified by passage to a later denominator.
